title: Trying to actually finish a game - Room For Ghosts
author: Wheelydope
selftext:
I've been working on a few games with AI over the last 5 months, and my ambitions for them have gotten pretty huge. I still want to make those games, but I wanted to see if I could actually finish something smaller before getting any further into them.

I had this idea last week for a game called "Room for Ghosts." You build a village and try to make wandering spirits comfortable enough to move in before they reach your hearth and put the fire out. Cozy village building with some tower defense pressure.

Claude did the initial build, then I went back and forth between Claude and Codex for changes and polish. My role has mostly been deciding vision scope, what I want, helping with art direction, play testing, screenshotting issues, and giving feedback. 

For anyone curious about the assets: a lot of the buildings and characters were made through AI-written Blender scripts. Some of the environment is from Synty assets I own. The logo and illustrated UI cards are image generated. Sound effects are from Gamemaster Audio's Pro Sound Collection, and the music is currently synthesized placeholder music, but I kinda like it. The trailer was put together with Claude using actual in-engine footage, including staged scenes and custom camera movements.

I've started getting feedback from friends, which has been helpful, but there's still some balancing to do. Hoping to get some more unbiased feedback.

It's a Windows demo right now:  
[https://rainyporchgames.itch.io/room-for-ghosts](https://rainyporchgames.itch.io/room-for-ghosts)

Would appreciate anyone giving it a go and telling me what they actually think. Especially where it gets confusing or boring.
